labels.note: External coverage is faithful: Fox criticism and non-salute claims (E14), the Pentagon/Kirby position that the VP need not return salutes (E15, attributed to U.S. News), the C-SPAN border clip (E16) and the DVIDS March 23, 2021 briefing page (E17) are all described accurately, and the 'misleading / deliberate refusal and dislike not determinable' verdict follows from E15 and is honestly hedged (REQ3 covered). The answer honestly says that the original source, and therefore any removed/added/reordered/altered segments and their times, cannot be determined from the examined material. Checked each sentence: E5 frame (viewed) shows a rocket ascending with a bright plume, 'SOURCE: NASA TV' caption top-left and NASA logo top-right at 24.024 s; E11 OCR confirms 'SOURCE:NASA TV'/'NASA' throughout; E2 gives 96.063 s and 1 audio track; E12 ASR processed 0.0-96.0626 s with failed_ranges empty -- all supported, and the answer correctly treats the NASA caption as a clue, not a matched original. Checked each sentence against the cited evidence. E17 (Guardian: Starship exploded after lifting off from Texas; debris near south Florida and the Bahamas), E19 (ABC: spun out of control, debris streaking across the sky) and E16 (CBC quoting the Bahamian government saying debris fell into its airspace) all support the event claims with correct attribution. The answer is properly hedged: it treats captions as labels and says the link between this video and the event is unverified. Small points that do not change the verdict: the frame shows one streak, not 'streaks'; 'night sky' is not checked explicitly (the sources say dusk/evening); and the answer does not mention that the Guardian watermark in the video matches E17, which is a conservative omission.

Everything the answer states is supported. The 92% match, B 18-92 s, the unmatched A 76.2-81.2 s tail and the A 0.8-2.3 s speed/backwards span all appear in E26/E46, and the E36 frame at A 80.747 s is indeed black, which the answer hedges correctly. This is also major. REQ3 is roughly covered: the answer hedges the tail and the short span and does not claim authorship, though it omits the ~0.5 s boundary precision.

labels.span: including a foreground person holding an object resembling a handgun｜people at the left and foreground appear to hold or point handgun-shaped objects
labels.note: E5 (14.633 s) does show several people inside a shop, and E9 (43.833 s) does show a dark figure lying on the floor with people at the left and foreground extending their arms toward it, so the scene layout and timestamps are supported. In both low-resolution CCTV-in-a-meme frames, though, I cannot make out any handgun-shaped object: the white-shirted foreground person in E5 is bent over with their hands hidden, and in E9 the left/foreground figures show only outstretched arms. The handgun claims are hedged ('resembling', 'appear to'), but they are what the closing 'apparent armed confrontation' inference rests on, so I rate this moderate-to-major rather than cosmetic. The limitations correctly concede that no shooting or injuries are shown. The frames also carry a caption ('Armed suspect robs convenience store, gets shot by every customer inside') and a 2017-05-31 timestamp that the statement leaves out; that is not an error. verifier-FP-pattern: hedged visual descriptions of tiny objects in low-res frames are hard to adjudicate, and a verifier could reasonably go either way.

E19 (dailymotion x66c1kl), E20 (roadiscalling daily-life-in-cambodia) and E21 (yourdictionary foghorn-leghorn-sayings) each match one URL exactly, each was acquired by SEARCH/open/http+trafilatura, and each returned text, so no opening failure appears in the cited evidence. The limitations cover both points (the embedded video was not inspected, and the readings did not exhaust the later text), and the statement makes no claim about the content. verifier-FP-pattern: meta/process claims ('opened', 'no failure recorded') flagged as unsupported_assertion even though one successful open card is cited for each URL.

Checked image E12 (low-res 240x180, zoomed): a dark-clad person near the top of the aircraft stairs has arms down at the sides, and uniformed personnel at the base, including the one beside the stairs and one on the left, have a hand raised to the brow in a salute. The statement is limited to this frame ('This frame shows no returned salute') and does not name the person or claim the whole boarding sequence; the limitations explicitly disclaim identity, date and behaviour beyond the frame. No overreach found.

Checked each claim against the cited evidence. The E15 frame (8.8 s) shows the lower third 'Transport Secretary / Grant Shapps MP' on Sky News, and the E12 OCR picks up that caption plus the ticker 'Transport Secretary Grant Shapps says all remaining COVID travel measures - including tests for arrivals to the UK - will end on 18 March'. So 'the broadcast identifies the interviewee as Transport Secretary Grant Shapps MP' is supported, and so is the attribution claim, which is scoped to Material A: nothing in the cited evidence names a 'Health Minister Jane Doe'. E19 says the remaining international travel restrictions, including the PLF and tests, are removed from 4am Friday 18 March, and E23 gives the page's declared publication date as 2022-03-14. The limitations honestly cover the unverified 'this week' timing and the fact that the video's own date is not established. verifier-FP-pattern: a scoped verdict ('false as a description of Material A') may be read as an unscoped world claim and flagged as unsupported_assertion/scope_overreach.

All six frame descriptions match the cited images: E15 shows the presenter with a gavel graphic labeled NEW LAWSUIT, E5 a paper-processing machine, E16 hands handling ballots, E17 a 'Now Processing: Ward 65' sign, E18 a person at a voting booth, and E19 a 'Statement from City of Madison' graphic attributed to 'Dylan Brogan, City Spokesperson'.
